name: Apostate
description: <name> was drawn to The Circle of Avalon. <name> had secretly despised sheepish, obedient Christians, and was relieved that others felt the same. [He/She] dreamed of Arthur’s imminent return from under the faerie hill, now that the purge was over.

name: Uprooted
description: <name> despaired. Seeing villagers die was bad, watching the <origin> sheep succumb was catastrophic. <name> did [his/her] best to ease their suffering - slitting their throats at any sign of infection. Without livestock or livelihood, <name> fled.

name: Caring
description: there was no one to tend to the animals. Hogs ran wild. Cattle starved in the winter fields. It was after <name> came upon a lifeless mare beside her newborn foal that [he/she] decided to shepherd whatever beasts were needful.

name: Cunning
description: <name> burned the putrid remains of [his/her] kin. [He/She] then followed the old grandmother deep into the forest. The cunning wicche knew every leaf, berry and fungus. <name> became fluent in the untamed language of the wild wood.

name: Rustic
description: <name> had learned to survive on foraged hedgerow fare, supplemented with the occasional stolen egg or trapped hare. <name> could make a meal from dandelion, primroses or stewed acorns. [His/Her] eyes were painful hollows, always hungry.

name: Soothsaying
description: <name> lived by the lore of oak, ash and thorn, trying to ignore the collapse of civilisation and seeking solace among the trees. [He/She] waited beneath hazel and hawthorn, listening for whispers from the fey folk. Sometimes, <name> was rewarded.

name: Spinning
description: <name> learned all about flax, for clothing, bedding, bread sacks, ropes and oil. [He/She] was soothed by retting and rolling, scutching and spinning. <name> had a steady hand, and eyes the pale, flaxen blue of a cloudless, summer sky.

name: Tireless
description: <name> got the knack of carpentry fashioning coffins for plague victims, later nailing whole families into their homes to die. Next, <name> built trebuchets in the War of Succession. Fac et aliquid operis, ut semper te diabolus inveniat occupatum!

name: Penitent
description: <name> acquired a cap marked with a red cross. It was a memento of months spent marching naked, one behind the other. Each whipped their naked, bleeding bodies with scourges spiked with nails. 'God is merciful, God is just', they wept.

name: Shrewd
description: circumstances could have been better, but [he/she] made the most of it. When <name> took to whittling amulets to ward against the Mortal Corruption, in a number of shapes to appeal to christians, jews or pagans, [he/she] got rich, fast.

name: Faithless
description: the priest beseeched <name> to repair <origin> church, despite the sickly season. [He/She] watched gloomily as the congregation gradually expired, sneezing as they broke bread together, and buried their brethren. God is dead, <name> thought.

name: Yorkist
description: <name> thought it was bleeding obvious that the royals were to blame, cutting England to the bone because of their silly French war. [He/She] had pitched in willingly to help shore up York's defenses. Someone had to make a stand.

name: Savage
description: <name> had utterly lost [his/her] mind. <name> had seen Beelzebub and there was no redemption. [He/She] could make shelter, and fire, and dream of blood and screams. <name> would not, or could not, say if [he/she] had eaten human flesh.

name: Cheerful
description: <name> would whistle as [he/she] worked, almost as though the horrors of recent times had passed [him/her] by. <name>'s reason to be cheery was simple enough. [He/She] had caught the pestilence, but had dodged the Grim Reaper. Life was good.

name: Charitable
description: <name> roved among the mills, begging or stealing flour to bake bread. This [he/she] made into simple bannocks and distributed to the starving village folk, barely clinging to the wreckage of their former lives. It kept <name> busy, and purposeful.

name: Avant-garde
description: <name> experimented. Have you tried rat au vin or eels in goat's milk? Neither had <name> until Armageddon. [He/She] was utterly fearless in combining random ingredients to keep everyone fed, leading to unexpected results and frequent indigestion.

name: Toxic
description: <name> fed a band of hungry marauders, a risky job. <name> would occasionaly cut corners to save time. Uncertain if it was a stray toadstool or mouldering rye that caused the hallucinations, <name> still maintained [he/she] did [his/her] best.

name: Clever
description: <name> believed [him/her]self spared from Mortal Sickness for a higher purpose. So said the Canterbury Friar, who taught [him/her] to read. “Knowledge is freedom”, <name> whispered softly, mounting the Friar’s mule and stealing away into the darkness.

name: Inconspicuous
description: <name> was deployed undercover to watch for heresy among royalist factions. On receiving no further instructions from [his/her] Master of Whispers, <name> sought the shadows, using what [he/she] heard to survive.

name: Ambitious
description: <name> crept about Oxford, tearing pages glowing with illuminations, swiping vellum and ink. <name> served [his/her] masters in the scriptorium dilligently. <name> had a steady hand. <name> would learn to read and write, and finally become Somebody.

name: Despicable
description: <name> took to the hills on a rampage as order crumbled. Born to privilege, <name> gathered a vile band of ruffians and killed and burned at will. [He/She] was exhilarated by chaos, amused by desecration, and not to be underestimated.

name: Accurate
description: <name> began to perform a sideshow, throwing daggers in an arc over a pretty girl for a few coins. <name> figured out [he/she] had a talent when [he/she] threw a carving knife dead into the eye of a looter. <name> never misses.

name: Confident
description: the noble's marches and forests became pretty much fair game. So <name> now poaches with impunity. [He/She] will catch what you want to order: venison, boar, rabbit, peacock. Naturally, this comes at a price.

name: Patient
description: <name> developed patience to sit in a furze bush or atop an oak tree, chewing on a blade of grass and listening to the wind. At the perfect moment, [he/she] would take down [his/her] prey with a single arrow. <name> had become an assassin.

name: Deadly
description: <name> was on a crusade to wipe out pretentious, usurping commoners and reinstate the true and righteous order of England. Blood mattered, and <name> would reclaim [his/her] birthright. The peasantry needed to be brought to their filthy knees.

name: Bloodthirsty
description: <name> recalled the healer lancing boils. Flagstones had run red as he opened veins, cursing the French, and the King. Finally <name> took the powders and purifying herbs from the dying healer's blackened hand. <name> was left holding the bloody razor.

name: Bookish
description: studying the many great works in the libraries of Oxford gave <name> confidence to try [his/her] hand at medicine. <name> was from a worthy family, the last of [his/her] name. Book learning surely surpasses base peasant cures, herbs and charms?

name: Hopeful
description: <name> fished leeches from the pond at <origin>, and carried them about in a milk jar, offering healing. <name> had no experience whatsoever, but had once seen a monk put the beasts on a dying man. It probably did no harm, <name> thought.

name: Ruthless
description: <name> recalled townsfolk dying in the streets as the nobles fled north to escape the plague. Are we not all mere sinners in the eyes of God? <name> would follow William of York in defending the rights of common folk. To the death if necessary.

name: Loyal
description: <name> pledged fealty to King Edmund, who was ordained to rule and bring England back into harmony and balance. <name> would gladly put anyone who disagreed with [him/her] to the sword. Death would be swift and merciful.

name: Chivalrous
description: <name> swooned over the histories of Sir Gawain and Sir Bedivere. To be so gallant, so merciful. <name> thought [he/she] had the right qualities to be a knight. And those qualities were sorely needed, in these savage days.

name: Weary
description: <name> was tired, truth be told. [His/Her] joints ached and [he/she] couldn't fathom how The End of Days had passed [him/her] by. <name> still oiled [his/her] blades, strangely envious of comrades slain at Saint-Omer. Somehow, <name> soldiered on.

name: Wicked
description: <name> regretted wishing death on [his/her] father's house. This very fate befell all [his/her] kin, and <name> was filled with remorse. [He/She] took up [his/her] father's hammer, and fired up the forge. Each metallic blow rang out: "Guilty, guilty."

name: Thrifty
description: <name> had left the silent streets of <origin> with a cart, and started collecting metal. From churches to manors, <name> stripped them clean and melted it all down. Sir Hugh Gaveston and William of York would surely be needing swords.

name: Tempered
description: <name> had packed [his/her] surviving children on a cart and fled. [He/She] could not remain, as the ghosts of [his/her] family would haunt the house for eternity. <name> found a niche as an ironmonger. Even the unhinged need new locks and bolts.

name: Brutal
description: <name> had fallen from grace, ending up in prison. Fate in the form of The Great Mortality - sickened guards and a filched key - offered a window of escape. <name> now had an unhealthy fascination with torture and tools of punishment.

name: Winsome
description: [he/she] became the Earl's lover. <name> had comforted him as his wife lay dying, and coerced him with blackmail when the countess unexpectedly recovered. <name> become a puppet master to the hapless Earl, his wife relegated to a distant tower.

name: Willful
description: bards told of how <name> commanded the barring of the gates, deaf to the pitiful wails and scrabbling outside. By sheer force of will, <name> kept extinction at bay in <origin>. That day, <name> became a legendary leader.

name: Artful
description: <name> chose eternal damnation over living purgatory. [He/She] sold the cow, then [his/her] only daughter. An artful beggar, [he/she] roamed the tattered shires, flattering, cajoling and seducing for a crust of bread. <name> is a survivor.

name: Crafty
description: <name> was scavenging from a bloated corpse, and came by a fine pair of shears. Trimming cloth from dead limbs was easy. Turning it into wearable garments took more practice. But <name> persisted. Now [he/she] can fashion a suit from almost anything.

name: Swindling
description: <name> raided barns for stray kittens and pups, fashioning brightly-coloured sacks from dead-men's cloaks to stash them in. Off to market! Jiggety jig. <name> would sell the unwary a pre-bagged 'piglet,' at bargain price...and vanish. Caveat emptor!

name: Thoughtless
description: <name> fancied [him/her]self a dressmaker. And so [he/she] set about using miller's floursacks, sheets and linen rags to clothe the destitute orphans and wastrels of <origin>. A frightful sight they were, shorn of their remaining dignity.

name: Reckless
description: <name> ventured into the abandoned mines, with a band of comrades and a few candle stubs. It only takes a pickaxe, any fool can do it, <name> supposed. And putting aside the fatal rockfall and the flooding incidents, <name> was right.

name: Desolate
description: <name> wanted to hit someone, to take out [his/her] rage at the horror and desolation that had violated everything [he/she] loved. But <name> was a pacifist. So [he/she] hacked spoils from the bountiful earth until [his/her] grief was spent instead.

name: Solitary
description: <name> had felt more at home in the quiet of the clay pits and lime kilns than in the towns. There were traces of humanity, but not the stench or the despair. <name> carved a secret labyrinth into the rock, invoking memories of Reims Cathedral.

name: Ashen
description: <name> had burned what could not be buried. Ash clung to [his/her] skin and throat until [he/she] forgot the scent of anything but smoke and death. It clings to [him/her] still, often in dreams.

name: Wary
description: trust was a luxury <name> could no longer afford. A smile could conceal a knife, a handhake spread a fever. [He/She] learned to remain vigilant, and to move before danger struck.

name: Tangled
description: the debts mounted quickly, and <name> tangled [himself/herself] in promises, betrayals, and desperate bargains. The plague wiped the slate clean, as there was nothing left, and nobody alive to pay.

name: Whole
description: somehow, <name> endured. Through fever, famine, and fire [he/she] remained whole - yet hollowed inside. Beneath the skin, grief festered, withering into a shape that only barely resembled [his/her] soul before.

name: Disciplined
description: with each blow and every struggle, <name> was hardened. Order became all that mattered. Without it, [he/she] believed, even the strongest crumbled into dust.

name: Gnarled
description: time twisted <name> like a winter-throttled oak. With scarred hands and a bowed back, [he/she] held fast to roots deep in the ruined earth of <origin>. Storms passed; [he/she] endured.

name: Frosty
description: <name> froze long before winter came. Each death, each burial dulled [his/her] spirit further. No comfort could thaw the frost that settled into [his/her] marrow.

name: Riven
description: the world tore <name> apart. Some pieces, [he/she] left in the mass graves; some, [he/she] buried deeper. Surely, once this harrowing was over, they had earned God's grace?

name: Seaborn
description: the sea could not weep, for it was made of tears. So, <name> raised a sail to ride [his/her] sorrow on salt and tide. Let the land rot. <name> would look to the horizon.

name: Frayed
description: hope unravelled stitch by stitch. <name> carried on anyway, patching the seams of a broken life with whatever scraps [he/she] scavenged among the ruins.

name: Candlelit
description: <name> often worked until Matins in the scriptorium at <origin> Abbey, illuminating documents by flickering tallow light. [He/She] befriended every pigment, coaxing gold leaf's gleam and verdigris to bloom. Silence was [his/her] companion, precision [his/her] obsession.

name: Merciful
description: <name> became adept with saw and iron, deftly cutting rot from living flesh. Some said [he/she] rather enjoyed it. [He/She] claimed it was an act of mercy, whispering prayers as limbs fell away.

name: Grim
description: <name> took no joy in the work, but neither did [he/she] flinch. Shackles clanked, keys turned, and bones broke where necessary. Words sometimes failed <name> - steel did not.

name: Singed
description: when sparks flew, <name> had been the first to haul buckets, drag bodies, and wrangle panicked beasts. The cleansing flames may have touched [him/her] here and there, but [he/she] was undeterred.

name: Unshaped
description: <name> had never liked drills or sparring grounds. So [he/she] was surprised to learn that when fists flew, [he/she] didn’t hesitate. <name> had finally discovered their own strength, yet knew nothing of discipline.

name: Gentle
description: <name> flinched at smoke and screaming, but never turned away from the wounded. [He/She] learned to stitch flesh, carving saints for those in [his/her] care. <name> softened the world to make the horrors more bearable.

name: Nurturing
description: <name> tended creatures and crops with quiet joy, coaxing life from egg and seed alike. Each act of care was a prayer for one of those who had perished before.

name: Studious
description: <name> practiced all arts with quiet focus, whether bladework or brushstroke. [He/She] had heard the pen was mightier than the sword, but opted to use both.

name: Lightfooted
description: <name> turned away from darkness. [He/She] had a ready smile, and would charm stories from the surliest of strangers, always chasing breeze over burden.

name: Keen
description: <name> studied tracks like an alphabet, and knew the signs to follow to avoid disturbing elves. [He/She] had witnessed many strange occurrences, but knew better than to speak of them.
